messages:
mike: quick check-in — thinking about migrating a subset of internal endpoints to gRPC + protobufs for perf and schema guarantees. proposal: start with the routing/quotas service. thoughts?
anya: :+1: agree on schema guarantees. two concerns: browser clients and polyglot services.
sam: for browser we can do gRPC-web + envoy translation at edge, but that adds proxy complexity. do we have capacity for that?
julia: also telemetry/trace propagation needs to survive the proxy. last time we lost span tags in the passthrough. sre-bot: incident note — 2025-03-12 regression when envoy stripped x-trace-id header, linked to config drift.
mike: good call. plan A: gRPC internal only, add gateway adapters for HTTP clients where needed. Plan B: full gateway-first with JSON->proto transpile at edge. A feels lower blast radius.
leo: prefer A. we can add an HTTP façade that calls gRPC on behalf of clients. keeps runtime simple and service code in proto.
anya: question: quotas are enforced at gateway today based on HTTP attributes. how do we maintain consistent quota evaluation if we move enforcement to gRPC servers?
sam: options: 1) keep quota at gateway (needs to decode proto or carry attributes), 2) enforce at service (need auth/tenant headers forwarded reliably), 3) hybrid (fast path at gateway, fallback service-side check).
julia: hybrid seems safest for rollout. gateway does cheap checks for most requests, services do authoritative check for v2 rollouts.
mike: rollout UX: canary gRPC rollout per-tenant. start with internal tenants only, then opt-in product teams. deploy-bot: canary created: canary/transport-migration - 10% traffic to gRPC for tenant region us-west-2.
leo: telemetry: let's standardize a proto header carrying trace/span/tenant in one place: x-rdw-proto-meta as base64 proto blob. envoy can pass it through unchanged. less brittle than multiple headers.
anya: agreed but we should avoid opaque blobs for observability teams. include plain headers for common fields (trace id, tenant id) and the blob for extensions.
sam: performance note — gRPC multiplexing and HTTP2 will reduce connection churn vs REST. we should benchmark with current 95p latency for small payloads.
julia: can someone spin a small perf spike job? I can add a dashboard tile. mike: @sam can you run the benchmark against a proto-only implementation on staging?
sam: will do today. rough script: ```bash
wrk -t12 -c400 -d60s --latency \ 
  -s ./scripts/grpc_bench.lua http://staging-internal-grpc:8080```
leo: about schema evolution — add field numbers and keep JSON compatibility by adding stable names. we should document migration rules in API Console.
mike: yes. docs + console warnings when someone pins a deprecated field. can we show deprecation alerts in the Console model catalog?
julia: product + devex can add a UI flag and a banner for owners. I'll file a card.
anya: one more: cross-language codegen. we'll provide generated clients for go/java/python/node. need CI to publish packages on change.
mike: ok owner list: mike (tech lead), anya (schema/compat), sam (bench + infra), julia (console/integrations), leo (telemetry). next sync Thurs. short updates in this thread.
deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/transport-migration -> staging -> us-west-2 (10% traffic).
sre-bot: monitor: error-rate spike threshold 1.5x baseline for 5m will auto-roll back the canary."
